newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva private bank launches cyberspace fund.
newsitem.headline: Geneva private bank launches cyberspace fund.

text.p: Geneva private bank Darier Hentsch & Cie said it is launching an investment fund to tap the world's booming information technology business, a first on Switzerland's estimated $1.8 trillion asset management market.
The open-ended equities fund, DH Cyber, targets a size of more than $100 million by the end of this year, Pierre Chevre, in charge of marketing at the bank, told Reuters.
"There's a lot of interest. This is the first investment fund of its kind launched in Switzerland," Chevre said.
Nobel Physics laureate Carlo Rubbia will be among a group of experts who will help Darier Hentsch manage the fund, for which subscriptions start on Wednesday and close on July 9.

The fund aims to cash in on a fast-growing telecommunications industry now ranked third globally in terms of market capitalisation, behind healthcare and banking, according to the U.N.'s International Telecommunications Union.

Chevre said DH Cyber will invest in shares of listed companies specialising in information technology products including semi-conductors, semi-conductor equipment, hardware and software manufacturers, computer networks and the Internet.
Two-thirds of the portfolio will be invested in blue chip information technology stocks such as Microsoft, Intel and Motorola and the remainder in companies with growth potential.
The fund is likely to have a big chunk in U.S. companies since the United States accounts for more than 80 percent of the world capitalisation of the sector, Chevre added.
